elaine: Throwing out a concrete attempt at a lightweight 'save-state hints' file for faster restarts / speculative warmup. Goal: let a node resume prefetch priorities without needing to reparse full manifests on every restart.

elaine: Key properties I'm aiming for: per-instance (not authoritative), best-effort (lossy), tiny on-disk, and abort-safe (ignored if checksum/mtime mismatch).

tomas: Sounds useful. Can you sketch on-disk layout? also curious how this differs from our previous hotstart cache ideas.

elaine: Layout sketch: small header + list of shard entries. Each entry = shard-id, last-read-offset (int), compact hot ranges (start,len) and a compatibility bitmask. Compressed with zstd for space. Example blob (pseudo):```{
version:1,node:"r-73",shards:[{id:"m-42",off:12345,hot:[[0,4096],[8192,4096]]}]} ```

kelsey: Nice. Two immediate questions: 1) what guarantees do consumers get? 2) how do we avoid stale-hint-driven IO storms?

elaine: Guarantees: none. These are hints only. Apply only if manifest checksum (or mtime) matches lightweight header. To avoid storms: rate-limit apply, cap prefetched bytes per shard and per node, and prioritize short ranges. Also prefer read-ahead of first N KB.

ryan: For interfaces, propose loader extension: ReadHints(path) -> (hintsBlob | Err) and WarmupPlanner.applyHints(hintsBlob) -> Plan. Keep it opt-in via config flag. Private deployments can disable.

elaine: + compatibility flag in header so older loaders ignore safely. Also include a short lease/epoch token so hints don't persist forever (TTL ~30s-2m).

kelsey: Operational metrics we should collect: hint_hit_rate, hint_apply_errors, prefetched_bytes, extra_io_due_to_hints, restart_95p_latency_delta. Deployers will want a dashboard.

elaine: Good list. Also track false_positive_prefetches (prefetches that didn't reduce RPCs) and bytes_evicted_soon (to detect wasted work).

ryan: Security/privacy: storing per-node progress may leak hot model usage patterns. For hosted, keep snapshots local and ephemeral. For Private customers offering central uploads, require KMS encryption and RBAC.

elaine: Agreed. Defaults: hosted = local ephemeral only; dedicated = local with opt-in central store; private = disabled unless tenant opts in with encryption.

tomas: Failure modes: stale hints ignored; hints too aggressive -> IO thrash; hints drifted -> no benefit. Mitigations = conservative defaults, canary rollout, and circuit-breakers.

elaine: Rollout plan suggestion from infra: feature-flagged canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% on dedicated clusters. Monitor metrics above. Deploy-bot: note: we should collect a short perf microbenchmark (restart latency, first-k-token latency, IO saved) and maybe an AB test.

deploy-bot: deployment note: plan staged canary. required metrics: hint_hit_rate, prefetched_bytes, 95p_tail_latency, io_ops_per_restart.

kelsey: Next step: small RFC addendum with API signatures, wire format sketch, metrics + rollout plan. Should we also include an opt-out environment var for node-level testing?

ryan: I'll draft the addendum. Will include pseudocode for ReadHints + ApplyHints and a tiny perf harness measuring first-50-token latency after restart.

elaine: Thanks all. @ryan ping me when draft ready and I'll review. :thumbsup:
